summary: Mobile SDK long-poll streaming intermittently egresses to US despite EU residency header
description:
Issue summary:
FinEdge reported intermittent spikes in end-to-end latency for long-poll streaming sessions from their EU customers. Client-side timestamps and server traces show some streaming connections are routed to us-east-1 (US) despite the token and SDK residency header indicating eu-west-1.

Impact:
- A subset (~4-7%) of streaming sessions initiated from EU produce p95/p99 latency spikes (handshake + initial token fetch) from ~80ms to ~850ms, and some sessions experience dropped streaming frames.
- Affects FinEdge production traffic (enterprise private tenancy) and increases cost and SLA risk.

Environment:
- Customer private deployment using Redwood Private with control-plane in eu-west-1 and edge proxies in front of regional serving clusters.
- Mobile SDK v1.4.1 (iOS/Android) with streaming enabled.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure mobile client with a residency-scoped API token (residency: eu-west-1) and enable streaming long-poll in SDK.
2) From an EU client network, start 1k short streaming sessions over 10 minutes.
3) Observe connection establishment traces in edge-proxy logs and control-plane routing decisions.

Observed behavior:
- Most sessions route correctly to eu-west-1, but ~4-7% route to us-east-1.
- When routed to us-east-1 we see TLS ALPN negotiation falling back and an extra SNI lookup, causing handshake delays and occasional 502s from the CDN.
- SDK telemetry shows a header value named X-Residency-Stamp sometimes serialized as an empty string or URL-encoded with a trailing space when the app prefetches endpoints.

Expected behavior:
- All requests with residency tokens and headers for eu-west-1 should be routed to eu-west-1.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- Edge-proxy (eu-west-1) trace: "route_decision: fallback -> us-east-1 (control-plane: stamp-empty)"
- SDK telemetry example: "X-Residency-Stamp: \"eu-west-1\"" and "X-Residency-Stamp: \"\"" (from same app build).

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Packet captures, SDK telemetry bundle, and sample timestamps attached to the ticket (uploaded to secure bucket).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: mobile SDK prefetch / connection warm-up occasionally strips or corrupts the residency header leading to control-plane treating the request as unpinned and applying fallback routing.

What we checked:
- Control-plane routing logs show requests with empty residency stamp are routed to nearest capacity pool (us-east in some tests due to edge-proxy topology).
- Edge-proxy config had a rate-limited path for warm-up connections which bypassed strict-residency enforcement for healthcheck-like sessions.
- Reproduced locally by running mobile SDK instrumentation with background prefetch enabled: when the prefetch thread raced with token refresh, header string builder produced a trailing space that URL encoding removed, resulting in empty header at proxy.
- CDN (third-party) will select a different edge node based on SNI and ALPN; extra handshake path shows ALPN negotiation to legacy profile when header missing, adding ~600ms.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Updated control-plane to treat empty X-Residency-Stamp as "treat-as-pinned" for the affected tenant for 48 hours (hotfix toggle).
- Instructed FinEdge to disable SDK prefetch in their next client hotfix as a short-term workaround.

Next steps and open items:
- Patch mobile SDK (PR referenced) to sanitize header construction and make residency header atomic with token refresh. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2184)
- Deploy edge-proxy config change to enforce strict residency for long-poll/streaming handshake paths globally after validation.
- Add unit and fuzz tests in SDK to catch trailing-space/encoding issues.
- Add telemetry in control-plane to count empty-residency-stamp events per tenant and alert at 0.5% threshold.
- Follow-up postmortem and customer communication draft.
